lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Pull a metal spring twice as far—and it pulls back twice as hard.

lines.speaker: skeptic
lines.text: A scrambled riddle? Prove your hidden law!

lines.speaker: hooke
lines.text: As the stretch, so the force—F equals minus k x!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: With his brass microscope, Robert Hooke peered into cork—and named its honeycomb rooms 'cells'!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Push a spring past its elastic limit—and it snaps forever.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tame that tiny hairspring inside a balance wheel—and humanity mastered portable time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Car suspensions, skyscrapers, even DNA strands today? Still obeying Hooke's law.
